reasoning: Governing allowables: yield gives 276/1.25 = 220.8 MPa for Al, 880/1.25 = 704 MPa for Ti (ultimate governs at 950/1.4 = 678.6 MPa), and 435/1.25 = 348 MPa for Steel. Bending uses M = 330 N·m at the 2200 N case, and deflection uses 4PL^3/(E b h^3) <= 3 mm. Checks use h minus 0.5 mm, and stock thickness and width are capped at 60 mm. Rough sizing: Al needs about h=16 mm, b=40 mm (about 0.26 kg); Ti needs about h=12 mm, b=58 mm (about 0.46 kg); Steel needs about h=12 mm, b=44 mm (about 0.62 kg). These are pre-checks for the specialists to verify.

notes.Al 6061-T6: Search thickness 12-16 mm with width up to 60 mm, since the 220.8 MPa yield allowable and the 3 mm deflection limit at 2200 N both drive the section, and h=12 fails at b=60 so the search should start near h=16 mm, b=38-42 mm. Verify REQ-006 at h-0.5 mm, and check h/b <= 2 for every candidate.
notes.Ti-6Al-4V: Stiffness governs because E=113.8 GPa and the 678.6 MPa ultimate-based allowable is loose, so search h=12 mm (checked at 11.5 mm) with b near 55-60 mm, where the deflection limit needs b h^3 >= about 87,000 mm^4. h=10 mm cannot meet deflection even at b=60 mm, so do not spend search effort there.
notes.Steel 4130: The 348 MPa yield allowable makes h=8-10 mm infeasible at b<=60 mm (for example h=10 needs b of about 63 mm at the 2200 N case), so search h=12 mm (checked at 11.5 mm) with b about 42-46 mm, and expect the highest mass of the three materials. Confirm REQ-003 and REQ-007 at the lower end of the width range.

I checked six Steel 4130 candidates. The lightest passing design is 15 mm × 20 mm at 353 g, not the 12 mm plate the lead suggested. The lead's h=12 mm section comes out at 622 g, about 75% heavier.

**Why thicker is lighter:** Bending stress is 6M/(b·h²), so the width needed scales as 1/h², and the section area (and therefore mass) scales as 1/h. Going from 12 mm to 20 mm roughly halves the area n

reasoning: Round 2 directive: Al 6061-T6, width 18 mm, thickness 25 mm stock (24.5 mm used as the REQ-006 worst case). Checks at P=2200 N, L=150 mm, b=18 mm, h=24.5 mm: sigma = 6PL/(bh^2) = 183.2 MPa; yield MS = 276/(1.25x183.2)-1 = +0.205 (meets the +0.15 target); ultimate MS = 310/(1.4x183.2)-1 = +0.209 (REQ-002 met); I = 22059 mm^4 and tip deflection = PL^3/(3EI) = 1.63 mm (REQ-003 met). REQ-004 (width 10-60, thickness 3-30) and REQ-005 (25 mm is a stock size) hold; REQ-007 gives 25/18 = 1.39 <= 2. The original 15 mm width gave yield MS of only +0.004 at 2200 N and 24.5 mm, which is why the width increase is needed. Ti-6Al-4V and Steel 4130 also pass the deterministic checks but are heavier (about 0.30 kg and 0.53 kg vs 0.18 kg for Al at this section). The Monte Carlo has not been run in this response, so the probability-of-failure <= 1% confirmation is still open and must come from the Al specialist before the design is released.

notes.Al 6061-T6: Search width 18 mm with 25 mm stock and check at 2200 N with 24.5 mm thickness: yield MS +0.205 against the +0.15 target, ultimate MS +0.209, and deflection 1.63 mm, which meets the 3 mm limit. Run the Monte Carlo on these inputs and report the probability of failure, which must be at or below 1%.
notes.Ti-6Al-4V: Yield margin is very large at 183 MPa against 880 MPa, and deflection would be about 0.99 mm, but the mass is about 1.6 times Al's (0.30 kg vs 0.18 kg). Keep it as a fallback only if the Al Monte Carlo fails the 1% probability-of-failure limit, and search the same 18 x 25 mm section.
notes.Steel 4130: Yield margin is about +0.90 and deflection about 0.55 mm, but the mass is about 2.9 times Al's (0.53 kg vs 0.18 kg) and it does not minimize mass, so it is not recommended. Use the same 18 x 25 mm section only as a reference case if Al and Ti both fail.

attacks.title: REQ-006 case: load +10% and plate 0.5 mm thinner
attacks.rationale: Combined check required by REQ-006. Stress_test: survives. Yield MS 0.595, ultimate MS 0.538, deflection 2.983 mm vs 3.0 mm limit. Passes, but the deflection margin is only 0.017 mm (0.6%).

attacks.title: Payload +25% (2500 N)
attacks.rationale: A heavier payload is a realistic change. Stress_test: fails. Deflection 3.142 mm exceeds 3.0 mm. Yield MS 0.477 and ultimate MS 0.423 remain positive, so stiffness governs, not strength.

attacks.title: Plate 1 mm thinner after machining (19 mm)
attacks.rationale: Machining or surface finishing can remove material. Stress_test: survives. Yield MS 0.666, ultimate MS 0.606, deflection 2.931 mm. Deflection scales with t^3, so thickness is the most sensitive dimension.

attacks.title: Arm 10 mm longer (160 mm) after layout change
attacks.rationale: A layout change lengthens the cantilever. Stress_test: fails. Deflection 3.050 mm exceeds 3.0 mm. Yield MS 0.731 and ultimate MS 0.668 remain positive. Deflection scales with L^3, so a 7% longer arm adds about 21% deflection.

attacks.title: Width 0.8 mm narrower (11.0 mm)
attacks.rationale: Width tolerance or machining loss reduces the section. Stress_test: survives. Yield MS 0.721, ultimate MS 0.659, deflection 2.696 mm. Margins drop but stay positive.

attacks.title: Fatigue at the clamp root
attacks.rationale: Cyclic bending at the clamp root, where stress is highest, is not modeled. The tool checks static strength only. Ti-6Al-4V notch sensitivity at the root is unknown, and no stress ratio or cycle count is given.

attacks.title: Stress concentrations at bolt holes or fillets
attacks.rationale: The model assumes a plain rectangular section. Holes or sharp corners at the clamp can raise local stress well above the nominal value and cut the margins substantially.

attacks.title: Dynamic or impact loading
attacks.rationale: The tool only scales a static load. Launch shock, vibration, or a drop event can produce load factors above the design value.

attacks.title: Off-axis loading, torsion, and lateral-torsional instability
attacks.rationale: The model assumes the load acts in the thickness direction. Any side load or twist adds torsion and lateral-torsional buckling risk, which REQ-007 (thickness/width <= 2) only partly covers.

attacks.title: Dimension and orientation ambiguity (11.8 x 20 mm)
attacks.rationale: The team's dimensions must be confirmed as width 11.8 mm and thickness 20 mm. 11.8 is not a stock thickness, so it cannot be the thickness. If the orientation is swapped, stiffness drops sharply.

attacks.title: Manufacturing tolerance bands and corrosion/galvanic coupling
attacks.rationale: The tool tests fixed losses, not tolerance bands or variation across the part. Ti in contact with Al or steel fasteners or structure can corrode galvanically, depending on the environment. Thermal changes also shift Ti-6Al-4V modulus and yield strength, which can alter deflection.

rationale: The selected 11.8 x 20 mm Ti-6Al-4V part passed the original envelope, but G-04 confirms that the 160 mm arm at 2500 N (the payload and arm change in the red team attack) pushes tip deflection to about 3.8 mm, over the REQ-003 limit of 3 mm, and the Monte Carlo (G-01) and breaking-point results (G-02, G-03) do not offset that deflection failure. The fix is within the envelope (width 10-60 mm and thickness/width <= 2), so another round of design changes can resolve it without escalation, and the risks in G-05 are carried as conditions.

summary: The bracket passes all six structural and factor-of-safety checks (S-01 through S-06) and the bare-metal finish, outgassing, stress corrosion, and buy-to-fly checks (M-02, M-03, M-04, F-01 through F-03), with the buy-to-fly ratio of 1.97 cited under F-02 as a cost driver. Open action items remain for allowables (M-01), dissimilar-metal galvanic control (M-05), fracture control classification (X-01), fatigue analysis (X-02), and the specialty metal, traceability, and supplier quality requirements (P-01 to P-03).
top_risks: Fatigue is not analyzed (X-02), so cyclic launch vibration loads are unverified despite the static margins passing (S-01 to S-03).
Design allowables are typical handbook values (M-01), so the margins rest on non-certified data until replaced with MMPDS A- or B-basis values for this alloy, temper, and thickness.
Specialty metal melt origin (P-01) under DFARS 252.225-7009 may constrain the supplier pool and schedule for the Ti-6Al-4V plate (F-01).

actions.action: Replace the typical values with MMPDS A- or B-basis allowables for Ti-6Al-4V in the specified temper and thickness, then rerun the margin calculations for S-01 to S-03.
Define the cyclic load cases, including launch vibration, and perform the fatigue analysis for the bracket.
Classify the part for fracture control (for example, non-fracture-critical) and record the rationale in the compliance file.
Specify fastener material and finish at the Ti-6Al-4V joint to prevent galvanic corrosion, per MIL-STD-889.
Confirm the melt origin of the specialty metal is the US or a qualifying country under DFARS 252.225-7009 before issuing the purchase order.
